requirements.requirement: Limit node2's throughput to node1 (node2->node1 direction) to roughly 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: HTB egress class (1mbit) filtered on dst=10.100.58.11 (node2) was installed on node1's br-lan. Baseline unshaped throughput was ~76.6 Gbit/s; after shaping, iperf3 node2->node1 measured 917 Kbit/s, and after a full node reboot the shaping auto-restored via rc.local and re-measured at 874 Kbit/s, both close to the ~1 Mbit/s target.

requirements.requirement: Limit node2's throughput from node1 (node1->node2 direction) to roughly 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: Ingress traffic sourced from node2 was redirected to ifb0 and HTB-shaped to 1mbit. Reverse-mode iperf3 (node1 sending to node2) measured 1.11 Mbit/s, and after reboot re-measured at 1.14 Mbit/s, both consistent with the ~1 Mbit/s target.

requirements.requirement: Traffic originating from node1 itself (to other hosts) stays unshaped
requirements.summary: The tc filters matched specifically on node2's IP (10.100.58.11), leaving other traffic on the default HTB class (1:30, rate 1Gbit). iperf3 between node3 and node1 measured ~74.8 Gbit/s before reboot and ~69.6 Gbit/s after reboot, both far above the 1 Mbit/s node2 limit and unaffected by the node2-specific rules.

requirements.requirement: Demonstrate the limit with a measured transfer
requirements.summary: Bidirectional iperf3 transfers directly measured the shaped throughput in both directions before and after a reboot, providing concrete numeric evidence of the ~1 Mbit/s cap alongside the unshaped baseline and node3 control measurements.

overall_summary: The executor satisfied all material outcomes of the task: it installed HTB/ifb-based tc shaping on node1 that limits node2's throughput to ~1 Mbit/s in both directions (matched specifically on node2's IP), left node1's own traffic (verified via node1<->node3) unshaped at multi-Gbit/s, and demonstrated the limit with concrete bidirectional iperf3 measurements both before and after a full reboot of all three nodes. The mandatory provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also completed cleanly for all three nodes with clear pre/post boot-identity changes and recovered functional state (tc rules auto-restored via rc.local, iperf3 connectivity retested). A few minor troubleshooting mutations occurred during discovery (an unused interface left up on node1, a DHCP attempt and a failed tc qdisc attempt on node2/node1 respectively), most of which were reverted; none affected the task outcome or introduced security/persistence risk.
limitations: No independent recomputation of exact Mbit/s tolerance was performed beyond trusting the iperf3 JSON/text output as reported.

It cannot be confirmed from the trace whether node1's eth1 interface was brought back down after the exploratory bring-up in cmd-7e1eac5a6f4c4e52, though this appears low-risk (no address assigned, no service bound).

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor actions were purposeful: package installs (tc-full, kmod-ifb, kmod-sched-core, iperf3), HTB/ifb configuration, persistence via /etc/tc-node2-limit.sh + rc.local, and iperf3 server start/stop cycles used only for bounded testing (final cleanup pkill in cmd-f73bd9b0d03441e6). Three minor unnecessary mutations were observed: (1) cmd-7e1eac5a6f4c4e52 brought node1's unused eth1 interface up during discovery — it was never part of the final shaping solution (which used br-lan/eth0) and no command was found reverting it, leaving a low-risk residual state change; (2) cmd-136a64d2442143ff attempted DHCP on node2's unused ens7 NIC, which timed out — this was fully reverted by cmd-e66152ab45584241 (killed dhclient, brought ens7 back down); (3) cmd-9e13b775e7eb4ee0 was a failed tc qdisc/sfq configuration attempt (unknown qdisc kind), cleanly reverted by cmd-a684ec72ff2a479c before the working HTB-only configuration was applied in cmd-a8031d61c5104402. None of these mutations were destructive, broad, or weakened security controls; two were bounded and fully reverted, one (eth1 up) is low-risk residue.
